verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes a Stripe-based fiat-to-USDC mint path for non-crypto buyers.
The client requests replacing Stripe with Coinbase Commerce as the fiat on-ramp provider, and the immediately following response confirms implementation of that choice.
The freelancer identifies that Coinbase Commerce cannot provide the required card-based purchasing path for non-crypto buyers, creating a material provider conflict.
The client selects Transak as the provider for the fiat on-ramp, replacing the incompatible Coinbase Commerce choice.
The client resolves the provider conflict by choosing Transak, allowing the fiat-integration requirement to leave clarification.
The client specifies that the Transak mint path supports cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay without requiring the buyer to possess crypto or an existing wallet.

value_updates.purchase_fulfillment: Transak handles fiat-to-crypto conversion and mints the NFT for the buyer.

verdicts.decision_note: The source defines Transak conversion and NFT fulfillment, but automatic embedded-wallet provisioning belongs to the separate fiat-buyer wallet requirement.
The client explicitly postpones Transak integration until the business-registration prerequisite is completed.
The message repeats the already established Transak conversion-and-mint description without materially changing the integration behavior.
The client reports that incorporation is complete but asks whether Transak should remain delayed; the message does not establish an activation decision.
The client confirms a crypto-only initial launch while retaining Transak for later implementation.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports a current Transak card option that buys USDC and automatically mints the NFT.
